(1) Sleeping area. The minimum occupancy area required by table 404.5 in this subsection shall not be included as sleeping area in determining minimum occupancy area for sleeping purposes. All sleeping areas shall comply with subsection (d) of this section.
(2) Combined spaces. Combined living room and dining room spaces shall comply with the requirements of table 404.5 in this subsection if the total area is equal to that required for separate rooms and if the space is located so as to function as a combination living room/dining room.
(f) Efficiency dwelling units. An efficiency living unit shall conform to the requirements of this article except as modified herein:
(1) The unit shall have a living room of not less than 220 square feet (20.4 m) of floor area. An additional 100 square feet (9.3 m) of floor area shall be provided for each occupant of such unit in excess of two.
(2) The unit shall be provided with a separate closet.
(3) The unit shall be provided with a kitchen sink, cooking appliance and refrigeration facilities, each having a clear working space of not less than 30 inches (762 mm) in front. Light and ventilation conforming to this division shall be provided.
(4) The unit shall be provided with a separate bathroom containing a water closet, lavatory and bathtub or shower.
(g) Food preparation. All spaces to be occupied for food preparation purposes shall contain suitable space and equipment to store, prepare and serve foods in a sanitary manner. There shall be adequate facilities and services for the sanitary disposal of food wastes and refuse, including facilities for temporary storage.
(h) Kitchen facilities. Every dwelling unit shall contain a kitchen equipped with the following minimum facilities and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition:
(1) Food preparation surfaces impervious to water and free of defects which could trap food or liquid.
(2) Shelving, cabinets or drawers for the storage of food and cooking and eating utensils, all of which shall be maintained in good repair.
(3) Freestanding or permanently installed cookstove. Portable electric cooking equipment shall not fulfill this requirement. Portable cooking equipment employing flame shall be prohibited.
(4) Mechanical refrigeration equipment for the storage of perishable foodstuffs.
Exceptions to the requirements of this subsection are as follows: Nothing herein shall preclude a written agreement between an owner and tenant that the tenant will furnish mechanical refrigeration equipment and/or a cookstove as required in this section. It shall be an affirmative defense available to an owner charged with a violation of this section if such an agreement exists.
(Code 1981, § 11-204; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 404, 12-5-2005)
422:
(a) Scope. The provisions of this division shall govern the minimum plumbing systems, facilities and plumbing fixtures to be provided.
(b) Responsibility. The owner of the occupied structure or his/her designated agent shall provide and maintain such plumbing facilities and plumbing fixtures in compliance with these requirements. A person shall not occupy as owner-occupant or permit another person to occupy any structure or premises which does not comply with the requirements of this division.
(Code 1981, § 11-251)
423:
(a) Sanitary facilities. Every dwelling unit shall contain not less than a kitchen sink, lavatory, tub or shower, and a water closet all in good working condition and properly connected to an approved water and sewer system. Every plumbing fixture and water and waste pipe shall be properly installed and maintained in good sanitary working condition free from defects, leaks and obstructions. All required plumbing fixtures shall be located within the dwelling unit and be accessible to the occupants of same. The water closet, tub or shower and lavatory shall be located in a room affording privacy to the user and such room shall have a minimum floor space of 30 square feet (2.8 m 2 ) with no dimension less than four feet (1,219 mm). Bathrooms shall be accessible from habitable rooms, hallways, corridors or other protected or enclosed area.
(b) Roominghouses. At least one water closet lavatory and bathtub or shower shall be supplied for each four rooming units and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(c) Hotels. Where private water closets, lavatories, and baths are not provided, one water closet, one lavatory and one bathtub or shower having access from a public hallway shall be provided for each ten occupants.
(d) Employee's facilities. A minimum of one water closet, one lavatory and one drinking facility shall be available to employees. Drinking facilities shall be a drinking fountain, water cooler, bottled water cooler or disposable cups next to a sink or water dispenser. Drinking facilities shall not be located in toilet rooms or bathrooms.
(Code 1981, § 11-252; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 502, 12-5-2005)
424:
(a) Privacy. Toilet rooms and bathrooms shall provide privacy and shall not constitute the only passageway to a hall or other space, or to the exterior and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(b) Location. Toilet rooms and bathrooms serving hotel units, rooming units or dormitory units shall have access by traversing not more than one flight of stairs and shall have access from a common hall or passageway.
(c) Location of employees' toilet facilities. Toilet facilities shall have access from within the employees' regular working area. The required toilet facilities shall be located not more than one story above or below the employees' regular working area and the path of travel to such facilities shall not exceed a distance of 500 feet (152 m). Employee facilities shall either be separate facilities or public customer facilities and shall comply with the provisions of section 2902.5 of the International Building Code, 2010 edition. Exception: Facilities that are required for employees in storage structures or kiosks, and which are located in adjacent structures under the same ownership, lease or control, shall not exceed a travel distance of 500 feet (152 m) from the employee's regular working area to the facilities.
(Code 1981, § 11-253; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 503, 12-5-2005)
425:
(a) Maintained. Plumbing fixtures shall be properly installed and maintained in working order, and shall be kept free from obstructions, leaks and defects and be capable of performing the function for which such plumbing fixtures are designed. Plumbing fixtures shall be maintained in a safe, sanitary and functional condition.
(b) Fixture clearances. Plumbing fixtures shall have adequate clearances for usage and cleaning.
(Code 1981, § 11-254; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 504, 12-5-2005)
426:
(a) Connection to public system or approved private system. Every sink, lavatory, bathtub or shower, drinking fountain, water closet or other plumbing fixture shall be properly connected to either a public water system or to an approved private water system. Kitchen sinks, lavatories, laundry facilities, bathtubs and showers shall be supplied with hot or tempered and cold running water, and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(b) Contamination. The water supply shall be maintained free from contamination, and all water inlets for plumbing fixtures shall be located above the flood level rim of the fixture. Shampoo basin faucets, janitor sink faucets, and other hose bibs or faucets to which hoses are attached and left in place, shall be protected by an approved atmospheric-type vacuum breaker or an approved permanently attached hose connection vacuum breaker and shall comply with the provisions of sections 609.12.1 through 609.14.4.2 in the International Plumbing Code, 2010 edition.
(c) Supply. The water supply system shall be installed and maintained to provide a supply of water to plumbing fixtures, devices and appurtenances in sufficient volume and at pressures adequate to enable the fixtures to function properly, safely, and free from defects and leaks.
(d) Water heating facilities. Water heating facilities shall be properly installed, maintained and capable of providing an adequate amount of water to be drawn at every required kitchen sink, lavatory, bathtub, shower and laundry facility at a temperature of not less than 120 degrees Fahrenheit (49 degrees Celsius). A gas-burning water heater shall not be located in any bathroom, toilet room, bedroom or other occupied room normally kept closed, unless adequate combustion air is provided. An approved combination temperature and pressure relief valve and relief valve discharge pipe shall be properly installed and maintained on water heaters and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(Code 1981, § 11-255; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 505, 12-5-2005)
427:
(a) Connection to public system or approved private system. Plumbing fixtures shall be properly connected to either a public sewer system or to an approved private sewage disposal system in accordance with the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(b) Maintenance. Every plumbing stack, vent, waste and sewer line shall function properly and be kept free from obstructions, leaks and defects in accordance with the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(Code 1981, § 11-256; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 506, 12-5-2005)
428:
The drainage from roofs and paved areas, yards and courts and other open areas on the premises shall not be discharged in a way that creates a public nuisance.
(Code 1981, § 11-257; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 507, 12-5-2005)
431:
(a) Scope. The provisions of this division shall govern the minimum mechanical and electrical facilities and equipment to be provided.
(b) Responsibility. The owner or his/her designated agent of the structure shall provide and maintain mechanical and electrical facilities and equipment in compliance with these requirements. A person shall not occupy as owner/occupant or permit another person to occupy any premises which does not comply with the requirements of this division.
(Code 1981, § 11-281; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 601, 12-5-2005)
432:
(a) Generally. Every dwelling unit shall have heating facilities which are properly installed, are maintained in safe and good working conditions, and are capable of safely and adequately heating all habitable rooms and bathrooms and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(1) Where a central heating system is not provided, each dwelling unit shall be provided with facilities whereby heating appliances may be connected, and shall comply with the provision of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(2) Gas heaters listed for unvented use shall be permitted provided the room heaters are installed in accordance with their listing and the manufacturer's instructions. Unvented room heaters shall not have a normal input rating in excess of 40,000 Btu per hour (11.7 kW) and shall not be installed in sleeping quarters. Exception: Listed unvented room heaters for installation in bedrooms shall not have normal input rating in excess of 10,000 Btu per hour (2.9 kW). Listed unvented room heaters for installation in bathrooms shall not have normal input rating in excess of 6,000 Btu per hour (1.8 kW).
(3) Gas-fired vented heaters installed in bedrooms or rooms generally kept closed shall be connected to an effective chimney or gas vent or equipped with a safety shutoff device. Gas-fired unvented heaters installed in bedrooms, bathrooms or rooms generally kept closed shall be wall-mounted.
(b) Liquid-fueled heating appliances. The use of any liquid-fueled unvented heating appliance shall be permitted in one- and two-family residences only, providing such appliance is tested and listed by an approved laboratory according to requirements of UL 647 (1984) and providing the fuel is stored in containers meeting ASTM ES-8 for kerosene containers and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(c) Commercial structures. Every enclosed occupied workspace shall be supplied with sufficient heat during the period from October to April to maintain a temperature of not less than 65 degrees Fahrenheit (18 degrees Celsius) during all working hours. Exceptions to the requirements of this subsection are as follows:
(1) Processing, storage and operation areas that require cooling or special temperature conditions.
(2) Areas in which persons are primarily engaged in vigorous physical activities.
(d) Room temperature measurements. The required room temperature shall be measured at a point three feet (914 mm) above the floor and three feet (914 mm) from the exterior walls.
(Code 1981, § 11-282; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 602, 12-5-2005)
433:
(a) Generally. Mechanical equipment, fireplaces and solid fuel-burning appliances shall be properly installed and maintained in a safe working condition, and shall be capable of performing the intended function and shall comply with the provisions of the International Building Code, 2010 edition.
(b) Equipment access. Access to outdoor mechanical equipment shall be maintained under all weather conditions.
(c) Cooking and heating equipment. Every dwelling unit shall contain a kitchen equipped with the following minimum facilities:
(1) Food preparation surfaces impervious to water and free of defects which could trap food or liquid.
(2) Shelving, cabinets or drawers for the storage of food and cooking and eating utensils, all of which shall be maintained in good repair.
(3) Freestanding or permanently installed cookstove. Portable electric cooking equipment shall not fulfill this requirement. Portable cooking equipment employing flame shall be prohibited.
(4) Mechanical refrigeration equipment for the storage of perishable foodstuffs.
Exceptions to the requirements of this subsection are as follows: Nothing herein shall preclude a written agreement between an owner and tenant that the tenant will furnish mechanical refrigeration equipment and/or a cookstove as required in this section. It shall be an affirmative defense available to an owner charged with a violation of this section if such an agreement exists.
(d) Flue. All fuel-burning equipment and appliances shall be connected to an approved chimney or vent. Exception: Fuel-burning equipment and appliances which are labeled for unvented operation.
(e) Clearances. AH required clearances to combustible materials shall be maintained.
(f) Safety controls. All safety controls for fuel-burning equipment shall be maintained in effective operation.
(g) Combustion air. A supply of air for complete combustion of the fuel and for ventilation of the space shall be provided for the fuel burning and shall comply with the provisions of section 701.2 of the International Mechanical Code, 2010 edition.
(h) Energy conservation devices. Devices intended to reduce fuel consumption by attachment to a fuel-burning appliance, to the fuel supply line thereto, or to the vent outlet or vent piping therefrom, shall not be installed unless labeled for such purpose and the installation is specifically approved.
(Code 1981, § 11-283; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 603, 12-5-2005)
434:
(a) Facilities required. Every occupied building shall be provided with an electrical system in compliance with the requirements of this section and section 14-338.
(b) Service. The size and usage of appliances and equipment shall serve as a basis for determining the need for additional facilities in accordance with NFPA 70. Every dwelling unit shall be served by a main service that is not less than 100 amperes, three wires, and shall comply with the provisions in section E3502.1 of the International Residential Code, 2010 edition.
(c) Electrical system hazards. Where it is found that the electrical system in a structure constitutes a hazard to the occupants or the structure by reason of inadequate service, improper fusing, insufficient outlets, improper wiring or installation, deterioration or damage, or for similar reasons, the city official shall require the defects to be corrected to eliminate the hazard.
(Code 1981, § 11-284; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 604, 12-5-2005)
435:
(a) Installation. Electrical equipment, wiring and appliances shall be properly installed and maintained in a safe and approved manner.
(b) Electrical lights and outlets. Where there is electrical service available to the building structure, every habitable room or space shall contain at least two separate and remote receptacle outlets. Bedrooms shall have, in addition, at least one wall switch controlled lighting outlet. In kitchens, two separate and remote receptacle outlets shall be provided (receptacles rendered inaccessible by appliances fastened in place or by appliances occupying dedicated space shall not be considered as these required outlets) and a wall or ceiling lighting outlet controlled by a wall switch shall be provided. Every hall, water closet compartment, bathroom, laundry room or furnace room shall contain at least one ceiling-mounted or wall-mounted lighting outlet. In bathrooms, the lighting outlet shall be controlled by a wall switch. In addition to the lighting outlet in every bathroom and laundry room, there shall be provided at least one receptacle outlet. Any new bathroom receptacle outlet shall have ground fault circuit interrupter protection.
(Code 1981, § 11-285; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 605, 12-5-2005)
436:
(a) Generally. Elevators, dumbwaiters and escalators shall be maintained to sustain safely all imposed loads, to operate properly, and to be free from physical and fire hazards.
(b) Elevators. In buildings equipped with passenger elevators, at least one elevator shall be maintained in operation at all times when the building is occupied. Exception: Buildings equipped with only one elevator shall be permitted to have the elevator temporarily out of service for testing or servicing.
(Code 1981, § 11-286; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 606, 12-5-2005)
439:
(a) Scope. The provisions of this division shall govern the minimum conditions and standards for fire safety relating to structures and exterior premises, including fire safety facilities and equipment to be provided.
(b) Responsibility. The owner or owner's designated agent of the premises shall provide and maintain such fire safety facilities and equipment in compliance with these requirements. A person shall not occupy as owner/occupant or permit another person to occupy any premises that do not comply with the requirements of this division.
(Code 1981, § 11-301; Ord. No. 2008-16, § 701, 12-5-2005)
440:
(a) Provided; maintained. A safe, continuous and unobstructed means of egress shall be provided. The means of egress shall be maintained continuous and unobstructed.
(b) Other standards and codes. Where the following provisions conflict with title 8, chapter 2, article 1 and title 25, chapter 2 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A. § 8-2-1 et seq., O.C.G.A. § 25-2-1 et seq.), the provisions of this article shall not apply. Such provisions of other codes and standards, which are found to be in conflict with this article, shall become part of this article and shall be administered and enforced by the city official.
(c) Exit capacity. The capacity of the exits serving a floor shall be sufficient for the occupant load thereof as determined by the city official.
(d) Minimum number of exits. Every floor area shall be provided with the minimum number of approved independent exits as required by table 702.3.1 set forth in this subsection based on the occupant load, except as modified in section 1004.2.1 or 1005.2.2 of the International Fire Code, 2010 edition. For the purposes of this division, occupied roofs shall be provided with exits as required for floors. The required number of exits from any story, basement or individual space shall be maintained until arrival at grade or the public way as follows:
Table 702.3.1. Minimum Number of Exits for Occupant Load
Occupant Load | Minimum Number of Exits
1—500 | 2
501—1,000 | 3
More than 1,000 | 4
(e) Single exit exception. An exception to the requirement of subsection (d) of this section is a single exit which is acceptable under any one of the following conditions:
(1) Where the building is equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system and an automatic fire detection system with smoke detectors located in all corridors, lobbies and common areas.
(2) Where the building is equipped throughout with an automatic fire detection system and the exit is an approved smokeproof enclosure or pressurized stairway.
(3) Where an existing fire escape conforming to the applicable codes and standards is provided in addition to the single exit.
(f) Arrangement. Exits from dwelling units, rooming units, guestrooms and dormitory units shall not lead through other such units, or through toilet rooms or bathrooms.
(g) Exit signs. Means of egress shall be indicated with approved "Exit" signs where required by other codes and standards. All "Exit" signs shall be maintained visible and all illuminated "Exit" signs shall be illuminated at all times that the building is occupied.
(h) Corridor enclosure. Corridors serving an occupant load greater than 30 and the openings therein shall provide an effective barrier to resist the movement of smoke. AH transoms, louvers, doors and other openings shall be closed or shall be self-closing. Exceptions to this requirement are as follows:
(1) Corridors in occupancies, other than high hazard occupancies, which are equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system.
(2) Corridors in educational occupancies where each room that is occupied for instruction or assembly purposes has at least one-half of the required means of egress doors opening directly to the exterior of the building at ground level.
(3) Corridors that are in compliance with applicable codes and standards.
(i) Dead-end travel distance. All corridors that serve more than one exit provide direct connection to such exits. The length of a dead-end corridor shall comply with the International Fire Code, 2010 edition, where the building is not equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system.
(j) Aisles. Arrangements of chairs or tables and chairs shall provide for ready access by aisle access ways and aisles to each egress door. The minimum clear width of each aisle in assembly and educational occupancies shall be maintained in accordance with the requirements of applicable codes and standards. In all other occupancies, aisles shall have a minimum required clear width of 44 inches (1,118 mm) where serving an occupant load greater than 50, and 36 inches (914 mm) where serving an occupant load of 50 or less. The clear width of aisles shall not be obstructed by chairs, tables or other objects and shall comply with the provisions in section 1004.3 of the International Fire Code, 2010 edition.
(k) Stairways, handrails and guards. Every exterior and interior flight of means of egress stairs serving any building or portion thereof and having more than four risers shall have a handrail on at least one side of the stair. Every open portion of a stair, landing, balcony, porch, deck, ramp or other walking surface which is more than 30 inches (762 mm) above the floor or grade below shall have guards. A101 Purpose and scope. The standards set forth in this section shall apply to the demolition of buildings or structures for which a permit is required under section 14-221(f).
A102 Definition. The term "demolition" means the act of razing, dismantling or removal of a building or structure, or portion thereof to the ground level.
A103 Time limit. Notwithstanding the provisions of the city's administrative procedures for the state minimum standard codes, the city official may impose a time limit as an additional condition of a permit for completion of demolition work once such work shall have commenced, provided that for cause one or more extensions of time, for periods not exceeding 30 days each, may be allowed in writing by the city official.
A104 Standards.
A104.1. Demolition work having commenced shall be pursued diligently and without unreasonable interruption with due regard to safety. It is the intent of this section to limit the existence of an unsafe condition or nuisance on the premises during the period of demolition operations.
A104.2. Any surface holes or irregularities, wells, septic tanks, basements, cellars, sidewalk vaults, or coal chutes remaining after demolition of any building or structure shall be filled with material as approved by the city official, and shall be graded in such manner that will provide effective surface drainage.
A104.3. All debris and accumulation of material resulting from demolition of any building or structure shall be removed from the premises.
A104.4. All building sewers shall be effectively plugged with concrete at the property line, or as may be required by the city official.
A104.5. Except where there is adequate space, or approval has been granted by the city official, the demolition of a multistory building by other than explosive means shall proceed with the complete removal of one story at a time. In the demolition of any building other than by explosive means, story after story shall be removed and shall be properly wet to alleviate any dust.
A104.6. No wall, chimney or other construction shall be allowed to fall in mass on an upper floor. Bulky material, such as beams and columns, shall be lowered and not allowed to fall. When any building over one story in height is demolished, precautions for protecting the public shall be taken as prescribed in chapter 33.
A105 Inspections. The city official shall make or cause to make the following inspections upon notification from the permit holder or his/her designated agent:
Initial inspection. To be made after all utility connections have been disconnected and secured in such manner that no unsafe or unsanitary conditions shall exist during or remain after demolition operations. In lieu of an inspection, the department is authorized to accept an affidavit stating that all utilities have been disconnected from said building.
Final inspection. To be made after all demolition work is completed.
(Code 1981, ch. 11, app. A; Ord. No. 2008-06, app. A, 12-5-2005)

496:
Bail, appearance and supersedeas bonds and similar obligations, shall be accepted and shall be forfeited in the municipal court in the manner provided in this article.
(Code 1969, § 11-40; Code 1981, § 7-20)
497:
It shall be the duty, province and responsibility of the arresting officer to determine the amount of bond on which the prisoner may be released. Such officer shall write in the amount of the bond (cash) in the space provided on the ticket ($_____) and that amount, no more and no less, shall thenceforth be acceptable regardless of who might suggest otherwise. Instead of a cash bond, a property bond in double the cash bond amount may be accepted on the responsibility of the person approving and accepting the personal property bond. The officer who receives the money in hand for the bond shall sign on the ticket and copies thereof in the proper space provided for bond receipt, and shall be held responsible to see that the money is properly accounted for to the city clerk and a proper receipt obtained therefor.
(Code 1969, § 11½-20; Code 1981, § 7-21)
498:
Upon the failure to appear of any principal in any bond or recognizance given by a person charged with or convicted of the violation of a municipal ordinance, or by a witness to appear and testify, the presiding officer of the municipal court shall proceed to forfeit such bond or recognizance in the manner practiced in the courts of this state.
(Code 1969, § 11-41; Code 1981, § 7-22)
State Law reference— Bond forfeiture proceedings, O.C.G.A. § 17-6-70.
499:
The city clerk shall issue scire facias on all forfeited bonds, recognizances or other obligations, returnable to the next term of such court at the usual place of holding said court, against the principal and the principal's sureties, which shall be served by the police at least five days before the return thereof, or if the party resides out of the state or county, scire facias may be served by publication, as in cases of scire facias to revive judgments, and if said party resides in said county, outside of the corporate limits of the city, the same shall be served by the sheriff or the sheriffs' deputy. If, at such return term, no sufficient cause be shown to the contrary, judgment shall be entered up against such principal and sureties or such of them as have been served; provided, however, if such bond or recognizance given is cash or its equivalent, upon failure of the defendant to appear at said court at the appointed time, judgment shall be entered up against such defendant, and the bond so given shall be forfeited.
(Code 1969, § 11-42; Code 1981, § 7-23)
500:
The principal or defendant then under conviction shall be rearrested by the police under proper order of the court, and the sentence or judgment of conviction carried out.
(Code 1969, § 11-44; Code 1981, § 7-24)
501:
Final judgments in all cases of forfeitures shall be enforced by execution issued by the clerk, bearing teste in the name of the presiding officer of the court, and shall be in favor of the city, and against the principal and the principals' sureties on said bond, which execution shall be turned over to the police for levy and sale.
(Code 1969, § 11-43; Code 1981, § 7-25)
504:
(a) Office created. There is hereby created the office of jailer.
(b) Appointment. The jailer shall be appointed by the city manager as provided by law.
(c) Bond. The jailer shall file a bond in the amount established by council conditioned upon the faithful performance of the duties of such office.
(d) Power of arrest. The jailer shall be a conservator of the peace with full power to make arrests.
(e) Control of prisoners. The jailer shall have charge of the jail and of all persons employed therein, and control of and custody of all persons lawfully confined therein.
(Code 1969, §§ 11½-17, 11½-25; Code 1981, § 7-30; Ord. of 11-11-1974, §§ 1—5)
505:
(a) It shall be the duty of the jailer to receive into the jail such persons as may be committed thereto by any court, police magistrate or justice of the peace in and for the city, or brought thereto by any peace officer, or committed by any court or magistrate in the county, by virtue of any agreement thereto with the city.
(b) The jailer shall require such persons to work at such labor as such person's strength will permit within and without the jail, not to exceed eight hours each working day, according to the respective sentences or commitments of such persons, and as is provided by statute.
(Code 1969, § 11½-19; Code 1981, § 7-31; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 6)
506:
The jailer shall maintain a proper record of the names of persons in custody and the amount of the bonds required to obtain their release. When a prisoner obtains sufficient funds to post the cash bond, the jailer may accept the same and sign the yellow copy of the ticket as receiving the same and release the prisoner. In all events a proper receipt for funds must pass in exchange for the funds obtained.
(Code 1969, § 11½-21; Code 1981, § 7-32)
507:
It shall be the duty of the jailer to keep a record of the names of all persons committed to the jail in a book kept for that purpose, showing the date of commitment, days of imprisonment, amount of fine and any other necessary data.
(Code 1981, § 7-33; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 9)
508:
It shall be the duty of the jailer to make out and deliver to the city clerk, on the first day of each quarter, a statement duly sworn to showing the names of all persons who have been confined in the jail during the quarter past, the date of their committal, by whom sentenced, the number of days sentenced, and the names of all persons discharged or released during the past quarter and by what authority they were discharged or released.
(Code 1981, § 7-34; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 11)
509:
All prisoners shall be relieved of any personal possessions on their person which might in any manner be hazardous to themselves or to other prisoners, or to the jail property during confinement, including moneys or other valuables. Such items shall be sealed in an envelope or other suitable container by the arresting officer and safely kept under lock and key for return to the prisoner upon such prisoner's release.
(Code 1969, § 11½-29; Code 1981, § 7-35)
510:
Whenever a prisoner escapes from the jail, it shall be the duty of the jailer immediately to pursue and retake the offender, and to notify the chief of police, giving such officer a description of the fugitive.
(Code 1981, § 7-36; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 13)
511:
The jailer of the house of correction may arrest, without warrant, any person trespassing upon the jail, or the grounds belonging thereto, or attempting to rescue any prisoner, or assisting or attempting to assist any prisoner to escape or hinder or attempt to hinder the jailer in the lawful discharge of such jailer's duties.
(Code 1981, § 7-37; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 8)
State Law reference— Aiding escape of prisoner prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 16-10-53.
512:
The jailer shall treat all persons committed to such officer's charge humanely; and if such officer shall assault, abuse, beat or otherwise maltreat any person in custody, or knowingly suffer or permit the same to be done; or if such officer shall supply any such person with any intoxicating liquor as a beverage, or knowingly permit or suffer the same to be done, or shall be guilty of any lascivious behavior, or other improper conduct toward any person in custody, or knowingly suffer the same to be done, or shall fail to supply each person in custody with a sufficient quantity of wholesome food or drink, at reasonable or proper intervals, or with necessary bedding, such officer shall, in each case be subject to a penalty of not less than $10.00 nor more than $100.00, and a conviction of any provision of this section shall be deemed cause for removal from office.
(Code 1981, § 7-38; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 14)
State Law reference— Cruelty by jailers prohibited, O.C.G.A. § 42-4-5.
513:
Whenever any person confined in the jail is or becomes sick, the jailer shall thereupon obtain the services of a physician for such person and shall then notify the city manager and police chief and shall see that the sick person is properly nursed and attended. Whenever such physician deems it necessary such physician may direct the removal of such prisoner to a hospital, but when such prisoner shall have sufficiently recovered, such prisoner shall be committed and required to serve out the time.
(Code 1969, § 11½-30; Code 1981, § 7-39; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 12)
514:
Visitors shall be permitted as much as 30 minutes at any one time of visitation in the hallway in the jail between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m. in the morning and between the hours of 2:00 p.m. and 4:00 p.m. in the afternoons. All other hours of the day the jail shall be maintained closed to visitors. Not more than ten visitors altogether shall be permitted in the hallway at any one time, and any of these may be removed at any time for good cause in the judgment of the jailer.
(Code 1969, § 11½-18; Code 1981, § 7-40)
515:
All persons sentenced to the jail or confined therein for violation of city ordinances, may, at any time before the expiration of their term of imprisonment, discharge themselves therefrom by paying to the jailer thereof a sum equal to the pro rata share of their fine for the unexpired sentence. All persons shall be promptly discharged upon payment made, as herein provided, or upon written order of the mayor in case of emergency only, or some court of competent jurisdiction, or upon the expiration of their term of sentence. Before any prisoner shall be discharged from the jail, on payment or otherwise, the jailer shall notify the chief of police of such intended release. All moneys coming into the hands of the jailer belonging to the city shall be paid into the city treasury.
(Code 1981, § 7-41; Ord. of 11-11-1974, § 10)
516:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Georgia Election Code, O.C.G.A. § 21-2-1 et seq.
517:
The city shall have and maintain its own system for the registration of electors. The city clerk shall be the chief registrar.
(Code 1969, § 2-71; Code 1981, § 8-1)
518:
The challenge of listed persons by other electors, shall be as prescribed in O.C.G.A. §§ 21-2-229 and/or 21-2-230.
(Code 1969, § 2-8; Code 1981, § 8-2)
519:
The entire city shall and does comprise a single election district.
(Code 1969, § 2-72; Code 1981, § 8-3)
520:
(a) Creation of position, appointment. The position of election superintendent is created. The election superintendent shall be an elector in the city and shall be appointed by the council, to serve at the pleasure of the council and until a successor is appointed. In the event of vacancy in such office for any reason, the city manager shall be the election superintendent. The term superintendent or election superintendent when used in this chapter shall have the same meaning as defined in O.C.G.A. § 21-2-2(35)(D).
(b) Compensation. The election superintendent shall receive compensation for such services, per election or primary. The amount of compensation shall be as established by the city council from time to time.
(c) Duties and powers. The election superintendent shall have all of the duties and powers prescribed in O.C.G.A. § 21-2-70.1, and such other powers and duties as are fixed from time to time by the council. It shall be the duty of the superintendent to prepare and publish, in the manner provided by the state municipal election code, all notices and advertisements in connection with the conduct of elections; to furnish the proper election officials forms and blanks, including tally and return sheets, paper ballots and other necessary forms, as required by law for the conduct of any such election; and to appoint an election manager and clerks and other poll officers for elections, and fix and pay their compensation for services. All primaries shall be conducted by duly qualified and registered political parties.
(Code 1969, § 2-66; Code 1981, § 8-4)
521:
The polling place for all city primaries and elections shall be the city hall.
(Code 1969, §§ 2-6, 2-73; Code 1981, § 8-5)
522:
The superintendent of elections, together with the city manager, shall cause such portions of the city hall as they deem appropriate to be converted into a place for casting ballots in conformity with the state municipal election code, section 34A-606.
(Code 1969, § 2-74; Code 1981, § 8-6)
524:
All ordinances, resolutions, motions and orders pertaining to civil defense, emergency management and disaster relief, which are not in conflict with this chapter, are continued in full force and effect. Such ordinances, etc., are on file in the office of the city clerk.
(Ord. of 6-26-2012, § 24-1)
526:
(a) Law enforcement. In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 38-3-4, the city police department shall be authorized to enforce the orders, rules and regulations contained in this chapter and/or implemented by the Alma- Bacon County EMA director pursuant to section 30-2(a)(4)a.1 or local governing authority during a declared emergency.
(b) Penalties. Failure to comply with any of the requirements or provisions of the regulations contained in this chapter, or with any Code section, order, rule or regulation made effective by the Alma- Bacon County EMA director set forth in section 30-2(a)(4)a.1 or local governing authority upon or after the declaration of an emergency shall constitute a violation of the provisions of this chapter. Any person who violates any provision in this chapter shall, upon conviction thereof, be punishable by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 120 days, or both such fine and imprisonment, for each violation. The owner of land upon which a violation occurs, and each person assisting in the commission of a violation, shall be guilty of separate offenses. Each day during which a violation or failure to comply continues shall constitute a separate violation.
(c) Injunctive relief. In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 38-3-5, in addition to the remedies prescribed in this section, the Alma-Bacon County EMA director set forth in section 30-2(a)(4)a.1 is authorized to obtain an injunction to restrain violation of laws, Code sections, orders, rules and regulations which are contained in the Georgia Emergency Management Act and/or this Code, and/or which are implemented by the local governing authority during a declared emergency.
(d) Enforcement. Except as otherwise provided herein, this chapter may be enforced by the city police department.
(Ord. of 6-26-2012, § 24-3)
